articles.title: 'They Are Alchemy' — Guillermo Del Toro Speaks Out on AI in Filmmaking and Why It Can't Replace Human Creativity
articles.summary: Acclaimed filmmaker Guillermo Del Toro spoke out about his thoughts on artificial intelligence and what he feels gets lost in the creative process when AI is used.
body: Del Toro popped into the r/movies subreddit for an AMA session with fans on September 9. One of these fans, going by the username ihs25ysf, asked him about some comments he’d made during a 2024 talk at the British Film Institute, where he said that AI can create “semi-compelling screensavers” and “that’s essentially that.”
“The value of art is not in how much it costs and how little effort it requires," he said at the time. "It's how much would you risk to be in its presence."

The Pan’s Labyrinth creator has been adamant that the human element of art be preserved — something for which he continued to advocate in his response to the fan, who asked him for his opinion on the “biggest thing lost” when a “computer generates an image instead of a human hand.”

To Del Toro, the “alchemy” of creativity and discovery humans experience when crafting a story or artwork is unachievable by a machine, and many of the best works are often elevated by "accidents" that happen during the creative process.
points: Acclaimed filmmaker Guillermo Del Toro spoke out about his thoughts on artificial intelligence and what he feels gets lost in the creative process when AI is used.

articles.title: The Best iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max Cases
articles.summary: It’s September, so Apple just had a huge event, where it released an annual Pro phone update in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. The standard iPhone 18 and follow-up to the iPhone Air didn’t make an appearance, though. Sorry, regular phone-havers, but you’ll have to wait a little while longer.
body: These new slabs of glass and metal are spendier than in years past, starting at $1,199 for the Pro and $1,299 for the larger Pro Max – a $100 price jump from their predecessors. Not that you wouldn’t have wanted to anyway, but protecting them is even more important. We’ve poked around, and picked out the best cases you can grab right now.

Your number one bet for an iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max case will be Apple’s first-party case. It’ll fit the best, and it supports both MagSafe and Apple’s Crossbody Strap and Wrist Strap accessories. The switch from FineWoven to TechWoven last year seems to have been the right call – by all accounts I’ve read, the cases have held up far better over the last year. The only things not to like about them, then, might be the look, as the colors haven’t gotten any more exciting this year. There’s also the feel; I’ve got issues with certain textures, and the TechWoven case gives me the creepy crawlies when I touch one.
The other thing to note is the price. Apple first-party cases don’t come cheap, and this year is no different. Expect to shell out $59 for the TechWoven case.

articles.title: Wardogs’ Massive Start On Steam Undercut By Brutal Server Queues [Update]
articles.summary: Update: A hotfix has now been released for Wardogs that targets the ongoing server issues. If you're logged in and stuck in a queue, you'll need to close the game to download the update, which will then send you back into a queue once you log in again.
body: More players will be let in as the issues are resolved, but no specific timetable is provided for how long that could take. Alongside the long queues, the patch targets issues with joining servers and an issue causing players to be kicked from matches.

"We will be actively monitoring the ongoing situation post hotfix and will be working through the night to see this resolved," the developer wrote in a post on Steam. "We apologize for the inconvenience this has caused."

Original story: A big new military FPS, Wardogs (not to be confused with the 2016 Jonah Hill/Miles Teller crime-comedy War Dogs) launched today in early access on Steam, and it's off to a hot start. The shooter reached 300,000 peak concurrent users on Steam right out of the gate and the $40 game is currently Steam's No. 1 best-seller. Pretty impressive for a game that the developer told you not to buy.

Given the flood of players, developer Bulkhead instituted a server queue system, and this quickly became something of a meme on social media. Players shared screenshots of the queue and their place in it--some people reported having more than 300,000 people in line in front of them. Yeesh.

articles.title: Call of Duty's Anti-Cheat Boss Dispels Cheating Myths, Breaks Down Review Process, and More
articles.summary: Cheating in video games has turned into a multi-billon dollar industry, which has forced franchises like Call of Duty to build entire teams to combat this epidemic.
body: IGN had the opportunity to sit down with Andrews and peel back the layers on Call of Duty's anti-cheat system, Ricochet. Andrews disspelled myths about Call of Duty's anti-cheat, offered clarity on the process of how they investigate suspected cheaters, how they've hired cheater makers to combat the problem, and much more. It's a rare opportunity, as there's a lot of caution around publicly speaking about anti-cheat in gaming. If you say too much, you could inadvertedly give cheaters a heads-up on how to evade detective, after all.

With that said, we drilled down on Call of Duty's long running issue with cheaters in an attempt to make it less mysterious. It's an important subject ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release in October and something Activision is working hard to spotlight.

IGN: Before we dive specifically into Call of Duty, tell me the difference between working on Grand Theft Auto Online, Red Dead Online, and Call of Duty, because one's obviously hyper-competitive, while Grand Theft Auto is a completely different ecosystem.

articles.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Recap and Review - The Once and Future Captain Kirk
articles.summary: In Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 8, “Orders of Magnitude,” Joe Morton is terrific as that classic style Trek guest star – the visiting Admiral who takes command of the ship – while Paul Wesley gets to deepen his take on the James T. Kirk that we know he’s evolving into.
body: Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 8, “Orders of Magnitude.”

And now we’re back to regular Star Trek again with this episode, after weeks of “concept” stories. “Orders of Magnitude” isn’t doing any gimmicks, even if it is trading on a tried-and-true set-up that Trek itself has tackled itself many times before – that of the increasingly erratic and dangerous commander whose questionable decisions put his crew into a moral quandary.

While Captain Pike (Anson Mount) and his away team are planet-bound and out of communications range, the legendary Admiral Simon Reeger (Terminator 2’s Joe Morton!) shows up in a shuttlecraft and announces that he’s taking command of the Enterprise. He’s uncovered a way to track a mysterious, cloaked enemy vessel that is believed to be responsible for something known as the Vardan Massacre, which resulted in 5 million civilian casualties. (The way he’s tracking it? The gamma ray burn-off from the ship’s impulse engines, obvs.) But time is of the essence, and so he takes command of the Enterprise while the trail is still hot.

articles.title: Amazon Prime Members Get Doom Eternal And 10 More Games For Free In September
articles.summary: The next wave of monthly games for Amazon Luna has been revealed, and if you're a fan of first-person shooters, then you're in for a treat. The headline act is Doom Eternal, or if you'd prefer your guns to be chatterboxes, you can also grab the delightfully weird High on Life.
body: Several new GameNight titles will also be available throughout the month, so if you're in the mood for some social gaming, you can check out kaiju-powered board game fun in King of Tokyo, test your general knowledge in Quiz Time: Guinness World Records, aim for a strike in Bowling Mayhem, and explore Cranium Planet.

As part of its September update, Amazon Luna is also introducing a Remote Play feature. This will allow people to play games together--even if they aren’t in the same room--and it should work nicely with the multiplayer titles featured in the Luna streaming library.

As mentioned above, you can download some pretty good action games, and if you want to experience the formative years of Doom, you can also check out the first two games in the franchise. Botany Manor is also recommended as it offers both a chance to flex your brain muscles and your green thumb. Rims Racing is a rock-solid motorbike simulator, and Just Die Already is an "old people mayhem sandbox game" from the team behind the Goat Simulator series. Several of these games are already available to claim, and the rest will roll out in weekly waves.

articles.summary: Borderlands 4 is getting a major content drop this week, and Steam players have a convenient excuse to jump into the looter-shooter without paying a cent. body: The free promotions include a mix of shooters, racing, strategy, and medieval multiplayer combat, so there’s a little something for just about every kind of player. And with Borderlands 4 at the top of the list, this is a particularly good weekend to see what all the fuss is about.

Borderlands 4 is available to play for free just as the game gets a major update and new content. Sept. 10 marks the launch of Story Pack 2, FL4K and the Last Resort, alongside Loveless the Hacker, the game's newest Vault Hunter. Loveless is essentially Borderlands 4 's answer to Borderlands 2 's Zer0, bringing stealth, sniping, melee attacks, status effects, and a murderous cyberworm companion to the game.

The other four games offer a pretty different assortment of genres and vibes. Surviving Mars: Relaunched is a slower-paced sci-fi city builder where you establish and manage a colony on the surface of Mars, while F1 25 is a racing sim built around the Formula 1 season.

articles.summary: Three years after its initial reveal, PlayStation and Haven Studios' heist shooter Fairgames (aka Fairgame$ ) has seemingly returned, according to a new playtest posted on Player.gg.
body: " Project Espresso is a third-person PvPvE competitive action game where competing teams race to infiltrate high-security locations, steal valuable cargo, and make it out before their rivals," reads the playtest's description on Player.gg. That sounds a lot like Fairgames, which a 2023 PlayStation Blog post described as "a thrilling competitive heist game where you join an underground movement to rob the ultra-rich and rebalance the scales."
Polygon has reached out to Sony Interactive Entertainment to confirm the identity of Project Espresso and will update this story when the company responds.

Fairgames (or Project Espresso, Break In, or whatever the game's final name is) will be the debut title from Haven Studios, which was founded in 2021 by former Assassin's Creed producer and Google Stadia Games and Entertainment head Jade Raymond. The Montreal-based developer was acquired by Sony in 2022, and revealed its long-in-development project in 2023 at PlayStation Showcase. Raymond has since left the studio.

articles.title: Netflix's New 6-Part Thriller Is 'John Carpenter Meets H.P. Lovecraft' With a Canadian Twist
articles.summary: That includes Calvin Penney (Josh Hartnett), whose family has lived in Snooks Arm for 40 years. Calvin uses his old fishing boat to gather chunks of polar ice after they calve off from glaciers and float south into Snooks Arm's waters.
body: You could say the fictional Newfoundland village of Snooks Arm is "dying," but in truth, it's been dead for a while. Climate change and overfishing have slowly stripped away most of Snooks Arm's reasons to exist. There's nothing left to do here besides leave, but some of the locals don't want to go.

But when Calvin's latest "glacier" turns out to be something else entirely, it's the first sign that something bigger has gone wrong in Snooks Arm. As the town warms up for what could be its last great festival, there's something new and dangerous waiting in the water just outside the village's light.

Below is a new 6-episode miniseries that's coming to Netflix on Oct. 8. Its creator and Canadian showrunner Jesse McKeown (best known for writing episodes of The Umbrella Academy and Letterkenny ) calls it " Jaws set in rural Newfoundland," where Snooks Arm is already in mortal danger from several different sources before something worse shows up. If forced resettlement, petty crime, or climate change don't wreck this town, there's something in the water that might.

articles.title: Dave the Diver has now sold more than 10 million copies, Mintrocket 'can't wait to share our future plans'
articles.summary: Deep sea exploration and restaurant management game Dave the Diver is still going deep: Developer Mintrocket says the game has now moved past 10 million copies sold across all platforms, while the In the Jungle expansion that came out in June has moved past one million sales of its own.
body: Dave the Diver was an " out-of-nowhere hit " when it arrived in 2023, earning a whopping 91% review score at PC Gamer—a site that does not give out many 90+ scores—and selling more than a million copies in just 10 days. A nomination at the 2023 Game Awards in the Best Indie Game category led to a small spot of controversy: Mintrocket is a division of Nexon, and so very much not an indie studio.

The overall impact seemed minimal, though, in part because Dave the Diver didn't win, but also because game director Jaeho Hwang has been pretty clear that he doesn't think of it as an indie game either.

The fact that Dave the Diver is a really good game that continued to get better with post-launch updates and crossovers that actually made sense is also probably helpful in that regard. In the Jungle, the DLC that came out earlier this year, is a banger in its own right: PC Gamer's Chris Livingston scored it a 90%, declaring it " just as charming and surprising as the base game."

articles.title: Virtue and a Sledgehammer hits different. We asked a neuroscientist to explain why.
articles.summary: But today, I’m in a rage room on Manhattan’s Lower East Side, living out my Virtue and a Sledgehammer fantasy. The upcoming narrative adventure game follows Pratelle, a one-woman army who’s out to destroy what’s left of her hometown in rural Spain, armed only with what she describes as “20 pounds…
body: I have never pulled a legendary sword from a rock. I have never been recruited into the yakuza by a grizzled hardass in a dank Osaka bar. It’s not often we get to act out the scenarios of a video game in real life.

I assume I’ll instantly unleash my inner beast in the rage room, but the reality is a little different. The space is tighter than I expected. The physics of it all are daunting to me at first. I whip a plate at the wall and it bounces back with only minor damage. Embarrassing! Eventually, I find my tool of choice, an aluminum baseball bat, and go to town on an LED TV. I bust through the screen and into the layers of plasticine sheets that form its innards, all the way down to the metal shell enclosing the back. By the end of just half an hour, I am pouring sweat and grinning like an idiot. It’s an unusually exhilarating Wednesday afternoon.

articles.title: Metroid Dread studio MercurySteam appears to confirm it's making Metroid Ravenous, addressing a lingering question from yesterday's Nintendo Direct
articles.summary: Spanish studio MercurySteam - the developer of Metroid Dread - seems to be the studio behind yesterday's Nintendo Direct showcase stopper, Metroid Ravenous.
body: Questions were raised after the Direct showcase because, despite the obvious visual similarities between Metroid Dread and Ravenous, MercurySteam's name did not appear in the Ravenous trailer or on any associated press gumpf. MercurySteam's social accounts were also quiet following the event.

I sought clarification from Nintendo and from MercurySteam this morning because of this, but heard nothing back - though this silence is not unusual for Nintendo, which often doesn't disclose developers until close to a game's release.

Nonetheless, MercurySteam appears to have ended speculation today by retweeting yesterday's Metroid Ravenous trailer with a ninja emoji and a heart emoji, presumably signalling some kind of stealth development situation. The same trailer was shared on LinkedIn by the company moments ago as well.

Metroid Ravenous seems to closely follow the Metroid Dread template, offering a side-on Metroid adventure, albeit one that plays with perspective a lot. Ravenous appears more colourful and less oppressive than Dread, and its montage of energetic gameplay lit-up Nintendo's Direct yesterday afternoon.

articles.title: Electronic Arts admits to using AI voices in NHL 27: 'This process allows us to bring more variety to the game'
articles.summary: Electronic Arts has copped to using "AI voice technology" in the upcoming NHL 27, saying that doing so will "bring more variety to the game" and allow it to react more quickly to changes and feedback.
body: The use of generative AI in NHL 27 was first reported by ESPN sportscaster John Buccigross, who also serves as the play-by-play man for EA's NHL series. "They're using some AI stuff now," he said on the Chirping Zebras Podcast last week (via IGN). "They played me some stuff back in my voice. It's like, wow, that's pretty good. If it means less work and the same check, I'll take it."
EA didn't respond to my inquiries about Buccigross' claim last week, but in a blog post shared today on the game's first update it confirmed that AI is in fact being used in the game.

"This process allows us to bring more variety to the game, react faster to league changes, and incorporate player feedback more quickly. Update 1 is our first step in an ongoing commitment to improve authenticity, with fixes for player-name pronunciations and repetitive lines. We will continue to expand player and city-name coverage in future updates."
The comment about fixes reflects something else Buccigross related about the process: The AI is sometimes off.
points: Electronic Arts has copped to using "AI voice technology" in the upcoming NHL 27, saying that doing so will "bring more variety to the game" and allow it to react more quickly to changes and feedback.

body: Marvel’s Wolverine certainly doesn’t skimp when it comes to violence, and gives you plenty of opportunities to enact it with style. But it takes more than blood to get my heart pumping, and it’s in Logan’s surprisingly nuanced tale of self-acceptance that I felt most connected to this latest portrayal of the most famous of the X-Men. That story is tasked with doing most of the heavy lifting here, with the initially slick and satisfying combat wearing thin well before its conclusion, but even that solid character work can’t quite carry the weight it needs to. Marvel’s Wolverine, much like its lead, is built on a firm skeleton, but what’s crafted around it isn’t nearly as strong.
